title: Navy court-martials two officers over 2024 capsizing of frigate INS Brahmaputra
dek: The warship's commanding officer is charged with hazarding the ship and the officer of the day with negligence, one report says. A sailor drowned when the frigate keeled over in a Mumbai dock.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Indian Navy has begun court-martial proceedings against two officers over the partial capsizing of the guided-missile frigate INS Brahmaputra at the Naval Dockyard in Mumbai in July 2024, one report said on Wednesday, citing a senior Navy official.

The proceedings against the ship's commanding officer, a Captain, and its officer of the day, a Lieutenant Commander, began in Mumbai on October 12, the official told the paper. The Captain is charged with hazarding a naval ship and with negligence in his duties; the junior officer is charged with negligence. If convicted, they could face penalties ranging from a reprimand or loss of seniority to up to two years in prison. The Navy has not made a public statement on the case.

The 3,850-tonne frigate rolled onto its side after a fire broke out on board while it was under repair in July 2024. A sailor drowned. The ship has since been righted and repaired, is undergoing trials and is expected to be seaworthy next year, another official told the paper. After the accident, the Navy set up a task force under a Rear Admiral to review safety on warships under repair, and its recommendations have been applied across commands.

It was the second such accident at the Mumbai dockyard: INS Betwa, a ship of the same class, toppled over during repairs in December 2016, killing two sailors. Three officers were court-martialled over that incident.

sources.title: The Hindu: Two Navy officers face court martial over 2024 INS Brahmaputra mishap
